'''Gulf Crossing Pipeline''' is a natural gas pipeline running from Texas to Louisiana.<ref name=source1>[http://bit.ly/2sBRQSA Gulf Crossing Pipeline,] A Barrel Full, accessed September 2017</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs from Sherman, Texas, to Perryville, Louisiana.

==Background==
Gulf Crossing Pipeline is an interstate natural gas pipeline fed from the Barnett Shale in Texas and the Caney/Woodford Shale in Oklahoma. It begins near Sherman, Texas extending to the Perryville, Louisiana area. <ref name = source3> [http://www.gulfcrossing.com/ "Welcome to Gulf Crossing"] Gulf Crossing, accessed January 2018. </ref> The Gulf Crossing system is composed of approximately 375 miles of pipeline having an average daily throughput of approximately 1.1 billion cubic feet per day in 2016. <ref name = source4> [http://www.gulfcrossing.com/AboutUsGC.aspx "About Us"] Gulf Crossing, accessed January 2018. </ref> Gulf Crossing interconnects with Gulf South Pipeline's Tallulah Compressor Station in Madison Parish, LA. It also has leased capacity on the Oklahoma intrastate system of Enogex, and on Gulf South from Tallulah to an interconnect with Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line's Station 85 in Choctaw County, AL, located at the terminus of Gulf South's 116-mile Southeast Expansion. <ref name = source2> [http://www.naturalgasintel.com/articles/19877-gulf-crossing-pipeline-open-for-business "Gulf Crossing Pipeline Open for Business"] Natural Gas Intelligence, accessed January 2018. </ref>

On 09 November, 2007, U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission published the Environmental Impact Statement of the then proposed Gulf Crossing Pipeline. FERC concluded that the project with  appropriate mitigation measures would have limited adverse environmental impact.<ref name=":0" />
